findings.reason: a wrong cause sends the census and the audit at the retired-exhausted cohort instead of the defective accepted cohort, and the remedy contradicts a policy the plan relies on.
findings.text: §35 states as cause "The edges are lost by identity changes", and requires "After repair, no live non-derived name lacks a DD source", over a population that is 91% (240 of 264) `exhausted`; the plan's own §31 (plan.html:221) records that an `exhausted` name with no incoming `PRODUCED_NAME` is claimed by the orphan lifecycle (`supersede_exhausted_orphan` in `imas_codex/standard_names/graph_ops.py`, whose cohort predicate is exactly `name_stage='exhausted' AND origin<>'derived' AND NOT EXISTS (source)-[:PRODUCED_NAME]->(name)`), so restoring DD sources for that cohort fights the policy, and an audit that fails closed on it refuses the release on names the lifecycle is retiring by design

findings.reason: without a control that the gate actually refuses a sourceless live name, §35's central guard is unmeasured and can pass while inert.
findings.text: §35's done-when asks that "the audit check exists and the release gate reads it", but the design bullet it is meant to prove promises the check "fails closed" and the gate "refuses while it reports any"; reading a check is not refusing on it, so a check that exists, is called and never refuses passes the whole section, and the only negative control §35 names covers the writer tests ("fails when it drops the edge"), not the gate refusal

findings.reason: a section this broad cannot be closed on one verdict, and its gate proves neither the writer fix nor the repair.
findings.text: §35 carries four deliverables: a census and cause trace, a per-writer code change so every identity-changing writer copies `PRODUCED_NAME` in-transaction (rename, fold, supersede, refine, create), a new audit check wired into the release gate, and a live data repair over 240-plus names including DD-path rediscovery and lead referral; each is separately gated and separately closable, and one verdict cannot cover the code change and the data repair together, exactly as §17 was split so each surviving row "becomes a section of its own" (plan.html:165)

findings.reason: the census and repair evidence would land at an undeclared path, which is the same defect an earlier review raised on §34 and the author acted on.
findings.text: §35's done-when ("the census names the dropping writer for each sourceless name … The audit check exists and the release gate reads it … no live non-derived name lacks a DD source") names no fragment or gate-log path, so the node chooses its own filenames and a later reader has no declared location to open, unlike §31–§34 which each name a `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/…` file

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `sn-review-through-jev` §5 resolves and its `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-review-through-jev/srtj-refine-ab-run.html` records exactly "62 of the 104 complete cases are dropped" for an unresolvable source; `sn edit --rename` resolves in `imas_codex/cli/sn.py`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §35's design promises an audit that "fails closed" and a release gate that "refuses while it reports any", but its done-when asks only that "the audit check exists and the release gate reads it", and its repair measure is escapable ("except those listed with candidates for the lead"), so neither the refusal nor the repair is shown to fire.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — §35's done-when names no durable evidence path for its census, its repair read-back or its gate log, unlike every sibling section (§31–§34 each name a `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/…` file), so a later reader has nothing declared to open.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §35 carries no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag into a symbol, file or comment, and its `implementable` declaration matches the vocabulary used by sibling plans (`sn-review-through-jev` §5–§7).
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §35 asserts the 264 sourceless names "are lost by identity changes" and sets an audit that fails closed on "a live, non-derived name with no DD source", but 240 of them are at `name_stage='exhausted'`, and the plan's own §31 records that a source-less exhausted name is the orphan lifecycle's intended target (`supersede_exhausted_orphan` matches exactly `name_stage='exhausted' AND origin<>'derived' AND NOT EXISTS (source)-[:PRODUCED_NAME]->(name)`), so for that cohort sourcelessness is the lifecycle's premise, not a dropped edge.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §35 bundles four separately gated deliverables in one section: a census/cause trace, a per-writer edge-carrying code change across every identity-changing writer, a new audit check wired into the release gate, and a data repair over 240-plus names with DD-path rediscovery and Jev adjudication.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §35 is declared `implementable` in `plan-section-declarations` and carries its own `<section data-reckon="section" data-id="s35">` element, so the roadmap resolves and can dispatch it; it declares no `depends-on`/`informs`/`gates` edge, and no declared edge points at the wrong node.
